figures.caption: Table 1. The three corpora and the trial phases analyzed. Trial counts per class are per participant. The KaraOne recordings contain 68 channels typed as EEG, six of which are not cortical.
Table 2. Processing and modelling stages, in the order applied. “Fitted on” states which data any estimated parameter is computed from.

Figure 1. The evaluation protocol. (1) The three corpora are analyzed separately. (2) Preprocessing is fixed in advance; the dataset authors’ cleaned epochs are used where a corpus provides them, and epochs are otherwise built from the raw recordings. The analyses above 45Hz use 256 and 512Hz versions of the data (section 3.3). (3) Every trial carries an identifier built from its provenance (corpus, participant, session, trial index, condition and prompt), and one module generates every split. An assertion halts the run if a trial is shared between sets, if the test participant appears in training under leave-one-subject-out evaluation, if a test class is absent from training, or if the validation set is empty; a split that passes emits a hash of its sorted trial identifiers. (4) Model selection, early stopping and thresholds use training data only, and the held-out test set is scored once. Every reported value then carries the statistics, shuffle-label control, measured detection floor and provenance record listed in the lower panel. FDR, false discovery rate; CI, confidence interval.

Table 3. Artifact controls on the three positive controls, within subject. Values are mean accuracy over participants, measured in this study. For ds003626 the decoder is EEGNet (F1 = 16, D = 4); for KaraOne and the competition corpus it is band-power logistic regression. The threshold is the exact binomial perparticipant threshold at α = 0.05. †Checked with its own shuffle-label control of 50 draws: the null mean lay between 0.2385 and 0.2409 against a chance level of 0.250, no draw reached the observed value, and p = 1/51 ≈ 0.020 in every case.

Figure 2. Overt-speech decoding on ds003626 from restricted channel sets, bands and trial subsets. Fourclass accuracy on pronounced trials, within subject, EEGNet (F1 = 16, D = 4). Each box summarizes the ten participants: the box spans the interquartile range, the center line is the median, the diamond is the mean, whiskers extend to 1.5 times the interquartile range and circles mark participants beyond them. Fill and hatching identify the group of cells. The dashed line is chance and the dotted line the per-participant significance threshold. The threshold shown is that of the full trial set; the trial-selection cells test fewer trials and have thresholds of 0.333 to 0.364. The cell that applies the dataset authors’ EMG criterion is omitted because it is available for only two participants.

Figure 3. Phoneme decoding in the KaraOne pre-imagery interval from channel subsets and single bands, for EEGNet (plain fill) and band-power logistic regression (hatched), within subject (top) and across participants (bottom). The rightmost group uses the 512Hz, 1–200Hz recordings. Each box summarizes the 14 participants, with the interval rebuilt as described in section 4.2, drawn as in figure 2. The dashed line is chance and the dotted line the per-participant threshold.

Table 4. Mean four-class accuracy on ds003626 inner-speech trials with an injected 8–30Hz desynchronization of increasing amplitude. Bold values meet the pre-specified detection criterion (mean at or above the per-participant threshold of 0.303, at least eight of ten participants above it, and group Wilcoxon p < 0.05). Band-power values at k = 0.05 to 0.2 are means over three seeds. A dash marks an amplitude that was not run for that configuration. Per-participant counts and p-values are given in supplementary table S1.

Figure 4. Detection of an injected 8–30Hz desynchronization in real ds003626 inner-speech trials, within subject (left) and across participants (right). Points are mean accuracies; marker shape identifies the decoder, and a filled marker meets the pre-specified detection criterion. The effect amplitude is the peak reduction of the ongoing rhythm over the central sensorimotor region, on a logarithmic axis with the no-injection condition placed at 0. The dashed line is chance and the dotted line the per-participant threshold.

Table 6. Smallest injected effect detected, by corpus, effect type and decoder, against the same cell without injection (paired Wilcoxon test, mean gain above one percentage point, Benjamini–Hochberg correction across all 240 cells). Amplitudes are peak values over the injected region in µV; nd, not detected at any injected size (largest phase-locking and coupling injections are given in the text). The Riemannian decoder is tangent-space logistic regression after principal component reduction and re-centering.

Table 8. Detection floors for the two validated phase feature families. k is the injected mechanism (lagged mixing fraction or modulation depth), not an accuracy. The last three columns are accuracy at the floor, accuracy with nothing injected, and the corpus’s chance level.
